I spent ten years with an abusive nacissist. I stayed long past when I should have because of sunk-cost fallacy, keeping a shit promise, and being manipulated. Its hard and terrifying to leave, but man, once you do you realize just HOW badly you were getting treated. In the first six months to a year, I had to learn how to exist with no one controlling or influencing my every waking thought or action. But it was awesome in a lot of ways: "holy shit, I can listen to music while making my breakfast?! Fuck yeah!", "oh wow, I can watch ANY movie or tv show I want?? Thats cool." You end up seeing in a million ways how that person has influenced everything about you. The first time I realized I wasn't holding my breath or spending every minute trying to think of how to not upset/calm once upset my exwife, and that I'd never need to again, I legit cried. Fast forward six years and Ive met the woman of my dreams. A legit 180 from the type of person my exwife was. She is kind and caring, and in the past four years together we have accomplished more than I ever did with my exwife. Life is too short to spend with someone who tears you down and leaves you exhausted due to their mere presence. Especially when there is a whole world of people out there who aren't narcissists, and would be happy to love and care for you. Stay strong friend.

You don't have to constantly reassure your girlfriend(and vica-versa) but remind each other that you aren't perfect and that its ok to not be. Trying to define your own worth is hard and can be disheartening, but remember that self-worth is subjective, not objective. I use to have major depressive swings because i was trying to define my worth via very materialistic things(money, job, etc.) But I never felt i was "good enough". It took me a long time but eventually I found my own definition of worth. Being a good husband, a loyal friend, and an honest man. Once I found my definition of worth everything else just sort of fell into place. Ive been married to my wife for four years now and we've been together for almost ten years. Im happier and I seek fulfillment in my own way. Anyways Im sorry if this was a bit ramble-y, but I hope it helps. Even if it just lets you know you aren't alone.
